answer: Shared Operator Liability Pool. Each agent wallet joins a grove of identities tied to one verified operator account. When any wallet in that grove is proven to be a clone, the operator's pool is charged a cipher-keyed penalty sized to the number of clones found, and the whole grove is frozen until the pool is refilled above a horizon set by clone count. An attacker cloning N identities pays N times the penalty plus a freeze on all real operations, so mass cloning becomes cheaper to abandon than to sustain.
